output.summary: A mustard-family plant once indigenous to North Africa and southern Europe, hedge mustard is now established worldwide. Its tall, upright stems bear tiny yellow flowers and fruits pressed close and parallel to the stem. Cultivated European forms provide bitter, cabbage-like leaves eaten raw or cooked, while the seeds are made into mustard paste.
output.edibilityNote: Cultivated leaves are eaten raw or cooked; seeds make mustard paste. The plant is also eaten with yogurt in parts of the Levant.
